memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a contrast when evaluating forward/input-gradient fusion; it does not establish that register pressure caused the measured timing.
memory_lessons.claim: The same-thread fused parent was correct and measured at 34.9285 ms, versus 35.4640 ms for baseline. This is a modest complete-call improvement, but the timing alone does not identify its cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare against a one-launch, path-specialized block-cohort variant that avoids carrying both accumulators in each thread.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured same-thread fusion is correct and modestly faster than baseline (34.929 ms vs 35.464 ms, about 1.51%), but it keeps two accumulators and two input streams live per output thread. This contrasting launch-fused variant assigns separate, path-specialized block cohorts to y and gx: it retains one launch while reducing per-thread live state, at the cost of duplicated coordinate/bounds work and twice as many blocks. Test whether lower register pressure offsets that duplicated work; timing for this candidate is not yet available.

retained: Replace same-thread y/gx accumulation with two path-specialized block cohorts dispatched by one kernel launch.
Retain the zero-padding bounds checks and FP32 accumulation order independently for each output path; each cohort freshly writes its output.
Leave the weight-gradient kernel and its launch unchanged.
